correctness.rationale: For a bouquet of k>=2 cycles with lengths >=3, an unselected spoke sees every selected hub spoke, so hub-spoke count can only be 0,1,2k. In every case omitted internal edges require exactly one adjacent selected edge; zero runs of the boundary-1 binary row are of length precisely two, giving F_n(z)=sum_j binomial(n-2j+1,j)z^{n-2j}. Hub boundary conditions yield G_1=z, G_n=z^2 F_{n-2}, J_1=1, J_n=z F_{n-2}, H_1=H_2=0, H_3=z, H_n=z^2 F_{n-4}, and the three-term bivariate product formula. Imposing nonadjacency on selected edges forces unique three-periodic patterns and the exact modulo-3 DIM formula, with values 0,1,2. Fresh independent direct edge-subset enumeration verified every bivariate coefficient on 93 ordered bouquets with 3..7 length petals and <=14 edges, totaling 1048 PED and 23 DIM sets. These bounded tests do not replace the unrestricted case split proof.

value.rationale: Single-hub bouquets are a natural cactus/GSP subfamily with interacting hub constraints. The explicit product factorization enumerates every size and hub-spoke refinement, and the sharp 0/1/2 DIM residue classification is a useful all-length structural theorem. Its value is not a new complexity result, and the known unrefined GSP total-count algorithm is conceded.
